source.title: Learning a Generative Meta-Model of LLM Activations
source.authors: Grace Luo; Jiahai Feng; T. Darrell; A. Radford; Jacob Steinhardt

page_placements.theme: Native neurons match or beat dictionary features on some tests, and much dictionary activity duplicates single MLP neurons

record.tranche_reason: The study probes individual raw MLP neurons for binary concepts, a different measurement relevant to whether neurons isolate concepts. It does not reproduce the pole audit or estimate the claimed shares.
record.gate_note: The reported 1-D probe scores for raw MLP neurons are included. GLP meta-neuron results are not results about the source LLM's neurons; dense probing uses many features together and does not measure single-neuron performance. Steering and activation-generation results do not bear on the listed neuron claims.
record.test_reason: The study trains a diffusion meta-model (GLP) on Llama residual activations and reports its own method's steering and probing performance. Raw MLP neurons appear only as a 1-D probing baseline against GLP meta-neurons. A best-of-thousands single-neuron AUC per supervised benchmark concept does not measure the share of neurons with one main job (V1/V2). It also does not test architecture or tool effects on interpretable share (V4), neuron circuits (V5), explanation validity (V6) or simulation scoring (V7). Bills et al. is cited only as standard practice for max-activating examples. It neither tests nor relies on the claim, so it does not test it.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that GLP meta-neurons isolate concepts better than SAE features or raw neurons, and that probing and steering improve with GLP compute. They note in passing that raw MLP neurons were the strongest baseline, indicating some native disentanglement. They make no claim about the share of neurons with one job.
record.recipe_differences: Uses held-out 1-D binary-concept probes of scalar neuron activations rather than pole-level human-readable explanations or an audit of job-count proportions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that probe scaling trends are cleaner with noisier GLP inputs (t=0.5) than cleaner inputs (t=0.1); this concerns GLP probes, not the raw-neuron results recorded here.

fits_no_version.finding: For 113 binary concepts, the best single raw MLP neuron gives average 1-D probe AUC 0.79 (Llama1B) and 0.82 (Llama8B). This beats SAE features and raw residual dimensions; the authors read it as some native disentanglement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For many benchmark concepts, some individual MLP neuron in a Llama model carries a concept-predictive scalar signal, outperforming single SAE latents on 1-D probing.

record.problems: The neuron evidence is limited to selected single-neuron probes on 113 benchmark tasks; it does not assess human-nameable job descriptions or quantify the proportion of neurons with one or multiple jobs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant raw-neuron single-unit results were reported. Dense-probing results use all available features together, and GLP meta-neuron results concern a separate model.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B pole audit and no job-count shares.
No shares estimated across models, architectures or scales; only Llama 1B/8B probe baselines.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
No test of architecture, regularization or tools on the interpretable-neuron share.
No attribution graphs or circuits built from neurons.
Max-activating examples shown only for GLP meta-neurons, with no test of explanation predictiveness.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked this as tests/T2, but every version is not_tested and the only neuron-relevant numbers are baselines for the study's own method. Reclassified as T4/cites_only. The citation of Bills et al. is methodological, not a test of V7.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B neuron poles, assign named jobs to poles, or estimate the one-job, two-job, and not-understood shares.
Does not estimate the claimed shares across models, architectures, or trillion-parameter scales.
Does not test InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons or recursive generalization.
Does not test the claimed effects of architecture, regularization, or tools, or the InceptionV1-sized model estimates.
Does not evaluate attribution graphs built from a model's own neurons.
Does not test whether explanations derived from activating examples predict where neurons fire.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating their activations on new text.

relation.reason: This is more than a citation: the study runs its own raw-MLP-neuron 1-D probe baseline and remarks that the LLM 'already exhibits some native disentanglement'. It never uses the finding as a tool, so uses_without_test does not fit either.

tranche.reason: T4 needs the study to use the finding as a tool, and GLP does not rely on LLM neurons being clean. Raw MLP neurons appear only as a 1-D probe baseline, plus a passing remark on 'native disentanglement'. So the study neither tests nor uses the claim.

source_check.notes: Both rows are best-of-512 selection baselines (Table 11: same as exhaustive search) in a GLP method comparison. They cover neurons of one middle-layer MLP only (8,192 for Llama1B, 14,336 for Llama8B per Table 12), not a share of neurons with one job. The authors only remark in passing on 'some native disentanglement'.

statements.correction: Table 4, averaged over 113 tasks: Raw MLP Neuron 0.79 [0.77, 0.82] (Llama1B) and 0.82 [0.80, 0.85] (Llama8B). SAE 0.70 / 0.76. Raw layer output (residual stream) 0.77 / 0.77. GLP 0.84 / 0.87. Best feature per task chosen from the top 512 candidates by val AUC.
statements.problem: none. Numbers and comparisons match Table 4. 'Best single' is a per-task best-of-512 selection (val AUC), at one middle layer only. For Llama1B the CIs of raw MLP neurons and raw layer output overlap.
